summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and prior left breast cancer presented for elective surgical correction of breast asymmetry and abdominal scar revision. She underwent a right breast reduction, left breast revision with liposuction, and abdominal incision revision with local advancement flap closure. The procedures were performed without complications, and she tolerated the surgery well. Postoperatively, she managed pain with prescribed medications, advanced to a regular diet, and ambulated without issues. A complaint of foot pain was evaluated with imaging, which showed no acute fracture but noted chronic changes. She was discharged home on postoperative day two with instructions for wound care, continuation of immunosuppressive and diabetic medications, a course of clindamycin, and follow-up with her surgeon. Her recovery was uncomplicated, and she was alert, ambulatory, and in stable condition at discharge.
